precepts.text: They that are delivered shall rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord in the places of drawing water; that duty stands even before all twelve tribes are gathered.
precepts.point: All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but we are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering; the body must move in one unison, in one direction, as a camp.

note.label: Numbers 4: The Service of the Tabernacle Done in Order

precepts.why:
The Lord referred to all the tribes together as the camp: the sons of Kohath came to bear the sanctuary “as the camp is to set forward.” If you are not in a camp you are out of order. People avoid camps because a camp carries a certain level of order and subjection, and they want to do their own thing, which is to sit in the midst of sin.

All twelve tribes are not gathered together right now, but the duty stands: “They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water, there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, even the righteous acts toward the inhabitants of his villages in Israel: then shall the people of the Lord go down to the gates.”

We are still commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, and that takes gathering. That duty stands even before all twelve tribes are gathered.

precepts.text: There shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord; the order of officers and judges is rehearsed in the body today.
precepts.point: Rehearse means practice, and practice makes perfect: there are rehearsals every day, classes and meetings for the men, the women, and the children, because this is not our rest.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

precepts.why:
“there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord”. Why does the body set up rank instead of saying I only follow Christ? Because we are commanded to rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord. All Israel stood before the ark in order, “their elders, and officers, and their judges”, half over against mount Gerizim and half over against mount Ebal, as Moses commanded. Reading the wars and works of Joshua, Moses, and the officers, judges and elders, we practice what our forefathers did, in order, as an organized army.

Rehearse means practice, and practice makes perfect. So there are rehearsals every day, classes and meetings for the men, the women and the children, because this is not our rest.

precepts.text: At the building of the tabernacle in the wilderness, both men and women as many as were willing hearted brought their gold unto the Lord; we have to have that same willing heart today.
precepts.point: Deborah and Barak sing praise to the Lord for the avenging of Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves. That is what the Most High wants from us: a willing heart in all that we do, in the keeping of the commandments, in the keeping of the feast days, and in the praise of him.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
Deborah and Barak praise the Lord “when the people willingly offered themselves.” The same willing heart was seen at the building of the tabernacle in the wilderness: “they came, both men and women, as many as were willing hearted, and brought bracelets, and earrings, and rings, and tablets, all jewels of gold: and every man that offered offered an offering of gold unto the Lord.”

That is what the Most High wants from us: a willing heart in all that we do, in the keeping of the commandments, in the keeping of the feast days, and in the praise of him. Men and women who were willing hearted brought their gold; the people in Deborah's day willingly offered themselves for the war. We have to have that same willing heart today.

precepts.text: Christ came not to send peace but a sword, to set a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him, and he that loseth his life for his sake shall find it.
precepts.point: How do we willingly offer ourselves to the Lord in the twenty-first century? By giving up whatever presents itself as an obstacle between us and the Lord. It may be father, mother, husband, wife, or children; it may be drugs, money, or working on the sabbath. If you willingly offer yourself, you will not let any stumbling block keep you from the Lord.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
How do we willingly offer ourselves to the Lord in the twenty-first century? By giving up whatever presents itself as an obstacle between us and the Lord. Christ laid it out: “Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.”

The obstacle may be father, mother, husband, wife or children. “He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.” It may be drugs, money, or working on the sabbath. “And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.”

If you willingly offer yourself, you will not let any stumbling block keep you from the Lord. “He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.” That is a willing people.

precepts.text: The one who cometh from Edom with dyed garments, treading the winepress alone in the day of vengeance, is the same picture the song is singing of.
precepts.point: The Lord marching out of the field of Edom, the earth trembling, the heavens dropping, and the mountains melting from before the Lord God of Israel is future prophecy; this has not happened yet.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
“Lord, when thou wentest out of Seir, when thou marchedst out of the field of Edom, the earth trembled, and the heavens dropped, the clouds also dropped water. The mountains melted from before the Lord.” This is future prophecy; this has not happened yet.

Isaiah sings of the same picture: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength?” The answer: “I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.”

His garments are red because “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment.” And the time is fixed: “For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.”

The one who marches out of the field of Edom in the song of Deborah is the one who comes from Edom with dyed garments, treading the winepress alone in the day of vengeance. The earth trembling and the mountains melting before the Lord God of Israel is that day.

precepts.text: Moses asked the Lord to set a man over the congregation, a man to go out before them and bring them in, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd.
precepts.point: Verse 9 proves it: my heart is toward the governors of Israel, the leaders who offered themselves willingly among the people. Her heart was with the men who led; she was not ruling over them.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
This passage is for all the closet feminists who think Deborah justifies women leading men. Look at the order the Most High set. Moses asked, “Let the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, set a man over the congregation, Which may go out before them, and which may go in before them, and which may lead them out, and which may bring them in; that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep which have no shepherd.”

A man goes out before the congregation and brings them in. Deborah did not lead men into any kind of war; she did not put on body armor and a breastplate, rise up on a horse, and lead the charge. She “arose a mother in Israel”, the motivating factor to men that were shaky and fearful during that time, a guiding light. Verse 9 proves it: “My heart is toward the governors of Israel, that offered themselves willingly among the people.” Her heart was with the men who led; she was not ruling over them.

precepts.text: The Lord answered in total agreement with what Moses spoke: take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit; the Lord set a man over the congregation.
precepts.point: Verse 9 proves it: my heart is toward the governors of Israel, the leaders who offered themselves willingly among the people. Her heart was with the men who led; she was not ruling over them.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
The Lord answered Moses in total agreement with what he spoke: “Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him.” Moses asked for a man over the congregation, and the Lord set a man.

That is the pattern Deborah fits inside, not outside. She was a mother in Israel whose heart was “toward the governors of Israel”, the men who “offered themselves willingly among the people.” The men governed and went out before the people; she did not usurp that.

precepts.text: The order did not change in the New Testament: the woman is to learn in silence with all subjection, not to teach nor to usurp authority over the man.
precepts.point: Verse 9 proves it: my heart is toward the governors of Israel, the leaders who offered themselves willingly among the people. Her heart was with the men who led; she was not ruling over them.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
The order did not change in the New Testament: “Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.”

So Deborah cannot be used to justify women leading men. She did not usurp authority over the man; she arose “a mother in Israel” and her heart was “toward the governors of Israel”, the men who led. The Most High set a man over the congregation in the wilderness, and Paul keeps that same order.

precepts.text: The account itself: Jael covered him with a mantle, gave him milk when he asked water, and when he was fast asleep and weary she smote the nail into his temples and fastened it into the ground; when Barak came, Sisera lay dead with the nail in his temples.
precepts.point: Blessed above women in the tent shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be. Sisera asked water and she gave him milk; then she put her hand to the nail and her right hand to the workman's hammer, and where he bowed, there he fell down dead.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
The song is singing the account of chapter 4. “Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said unto him, Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not. And when he had turned in unto her into the tent, she covered him with a mantle.” He asked, “Give me, I pray thee, a little water to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him.” That is the song's “He asked water, and she gave him milk.”

Sisera told her to stand in the door and say no man was there. “Then Jael Heber’s wife took a nail of the tent, and took an hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground: for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died.” That is the hand to the nail and the right hand to the workmen's hammer, and “where he bowed, there he fell down dead.”

Then, “as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him, Come, and I will shew thee the man whom thou seekest. And when he came into her tent, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the nail was in his temples.” For this she is “Blessed above women”, “blessed shall she be above women in the tent.”

precepts.text: In the places of drawing water they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, as we do in captivity.
precepts.point: Solomon confessed that the house he built was great, for great is our God above all gods, yet the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Him. He asked Huram for a cunning man to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, and colored cloth, and for cedar, fir, and algum trees out of Lebanon, promising wheat, barley, wine, and oil to the hewers.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House

precepts.why:
“They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water, there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, even the righteous acts toward the inhabitants of his villages in Israel.”

The offerings Solomon named, “morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of the Lord our God”, are “an ordinance for ever to Israel.” That is why we keep them in the land of our captivity: in the places of drawing water we rehearse the righteous acts of the Most High, according to the law given through Moses.

precepts.text: Even Deborah, who arose a mother in Israel, set her heart toward the governors and worked with the men of Israel rather than ruling over them.
precepts.point: Before a king is set in his position he is under tutors and governors; young Joash was king in rank, yet he was still a learner under Jehoiada, for even kings had to be taught. Athaliah had no place ruling Israel; being the king's mother did not make her the ruler.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 23: Jehoiada Anoints Joash and Athaliah Is Slain

precepts.why:
Deborah speaks of a time when “The inhabitants of the villages ceased, they ceased in Israel, until that I Deborah arose, that I arose a mother in Israel.” She arose a mother in Israel, yet she set her heart toward the governors and worked with the men of Israel rather than ruling over them.

That is the measure for Athaliah. Being the king’s mother did not make her the ruler, and she had no place ruling Israel. Even Deborah, a mother in Israel, did not take the rule over the men.

So when Jehoiada made the covenant “between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the Lord’s people”, and set Joash “upon the throne of the kingdom”, order was restored. Joash was king in rank, yet still a learner under Jehoiada, for before a king is set in his position he is under tutors and governors; even kings had to be taught. And once Athaliah was slain, “all the people of the land rejoiced: and the city was quiet.”

precepts.text: Those delivered from the noise of the archers shall rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, meaning we practice now how we will play when it is game time in the wilderness.
precepts.point: The way you rehearse and practice now is how you will play in the wilderness, and Christ can read minds, so those who are fronting, faking, and holding secret hate may be purged out and called rebels.

note.label: Ezekiel 20: I Will Not Be Inquired Of

precepts.why:
“They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water, there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord”. Rehearse. The way you rehearse and practice now is how you will play when it is game time in the wilderness.

The Most High will bring us out from the people, gather us out of the countries, separate us from the heathen we wanted to be like, and bring us “into the wilderness of the people”, where He will “plead with you face to face” and teach us everything we do not yet know of this Bible. Pleaded means what it meant for our fathers: “Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I plead with you”. He put them to death there, and it will be the same when we go back to the wilderness. With a mighty hand, a stretched out arm and fury poured out He will rule, which means two-thirds of us must go for the Most High to rule, and that is prophesied.

He causes us to pass under the rod and brings us into the bond of the covenant, and He will “purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me”. Christ can read minds. Those who are fronting, faking and holding secret hate may be purged out and called rebels, and “they shall not enter into the land of Israel”. So rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord now.
